clue.text: Military bases around both ends of enormous woodlands

indicators.note: around says the military bases enclose the other letters

parts.note: forts are fortified military bases

indicators.note: both ends of picks out the first and last letters of the word enormous

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Army camps encircle huge tracts of woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Forests are large areas covered with trees, the plural matching woodlands as a synonym.

clue.text: Loud reprimand for lacking courage

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
an earful is a scolding, a reprimand

explanation.surface: A noisy telling-off for being cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fearful is timid and afraid, so they lack the bravery that courage names.

clue.text: Soldier's gun almost left in seat

definitions.note: read as soldier is, so the answer names a soldier

indicators.note: in says these letters sit inside the word for seat

parts.note: the rear is the seat, one's bottom

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the word gun is dropped

parts.note: the word itself, cut short

explanation.surface: A soldier's weapon has nearly been left on a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional soldier in a standing army, as opposed to a reservist or volunteer.

clue.text: What Rory McIlroy does primarily struggle with in golf?

indicators.note: primarily says to take the first letter of the word struggle

parts.note: its first letter
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A question asking what the golfer struggles with most in his game.
explanation.walkthrough: Rory McIlroy is a star golfer from Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's swing is the stroke motion of the club, so it is what the player performs at every shot.

clue.text: Well I never did badly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, like 'Really?'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well I never did' is a whole exclamation of surprise, not a confession of doing badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Seriously! expresses astonishment, and seriously as an adverb means gravely, as in badly hurt.

clue.text: Bats — small fliers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: crazy people, ... being slang for those who are bats, mad

explanation.walkthrough: Bats look like the flying mammals, but here the word means crazy, and cuckoo is slang for crazy too.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo is slang for mad, as is bats, and cuckoos are also modest-sized birds that fly.

clue.text: One who killed his brother outside bishop's little house

indicators.note: outside says Cain's letters go round the other letter

parts.note: in the Bible, Cain murdered his brother Abel
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A fratricide lurks outside the bishop's cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is a small, simple dwelling such as a hut, which is a little house.

clue.text: Wound up about odd clue formed without noun

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: without here means outside, so those letters go round the next one
formed says the letters of odd clue are shaped into a new order

parts.note: N is the grammar abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: A setter finished up with a strange clue that had no noun in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside: OCLUDED, the rearranged odd clue, is placed round N.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind up a meeting is to bring it to an end, so wound up means finished or ended.

clue.text: Policeman perhaps unfriendly then more pleasant — though not at first

parts.note: off can mean cool or unfriendly in manner

indicators.note: not at first says the first letter of the word for more pleasant is dropped

parts.note: nicer means more pleasant

explanation.surface: A police officer who is at first frosty, then turns friendlier.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer is a member of a police force, and perhaps flags a policeman as just one example.

clue.text: Reaches agreement about former tennis player keeping dry

indicators.note: keeping says Seles holds the letters for dry inside

parts.note: Monica Seles, the retired tennis champion
TT is teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol, so dry

explanation.surface: A retired tennis star who stays off the drink comes to terms in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a matter is to resolve it by mutual consent, so settles means comes to an accord on it.

clue.text: New earring American increasingly bent out of shape

definitions.text: American increasingly bent out of shape
definitions.note: bent out of shape is American slang for annoyed, so increasingly so is a comparative

indicators.note: new says the letters of earring are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A novel piece of jewellery that has been increasingly twisted out of its form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent out of shape' is US slang for upset, which is why 'American' sits in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bent out of shape is US slang for being cross, so more so is a comparative of irate.

clue.text: Reward complaint about new information technology

indicators.note: about says the complaint goes round the letter for new

parts.note: a beef is slang for a grievance

explanation.surface: Someone is rewarded for griping about the latest computer systems.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is an advantage or payment given, so it works as a reward, a near synonym.

clue.text: Adult stuffed grouse by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: stuffed means full, and to grouse is to groan, giving full groan

explanation.surface: A mature game bird stuffed for the table, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Grouse looks like the game bird, but here it is the verb meaning complain, which is to groan.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something fully grown has reached maturity, which is what being an adult means.

clue.text: Pub's faithful having a change of heart

definitions.note: read as pub is, so the answer names a pub

indicators.note: a change of heart says the middle letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: loyal means faithful

explanation.surface: The regulars at the pub have changed their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of LOYAL is its middle Y, which is changed to C.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is British slang for the pub nearest one's home, the one regularly drunk in.

clue.text: Where one might have seen Botham and peers?

definitions.text: Where one might have seen Botham
definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., the London cricket ground where England cricketer Ian Botham played
second meaning: peers of the realm

explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London, home of English cricket; Ian Botham was a star England all-rounder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord's is the cricket ground, and lords are members of the British peerage, the House of Lords.

clue.text: What chemists may get from mixing answers

definitions.text: What chemists may get from mixing
definitions.meaning: first meaning: liquids with substances dissolved in them
second meaning: ... to problems or puzzles

explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the chemistry sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a solution is a homogeneous mixture of a solute dissolved in a solvent; it also means the answer to a problem.

clue.text: Dad's rants about principles

indicators.note: about here means in disorder, so the letters of the words are thrown around

explanation.surface: Father goes on at length about his moral values.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards are moral norms of behaviour, which is what principles are; a synonym.

clue.text: Spoke to a daughter then put clothes on

parts.note: to dress is to put clothes on, here past tense

explanation.surface: A parent talks to a girl, then she gets dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To address someone is to speak to them directly, so addressed means talked to them.

clue.text: Showed Democrat is engaged in fun activity

parts.note: to play is to engage in fun activity, so in the past tense played

explanation.surface: A politician shows off by taking part in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something is to put it on show, so displayed is the past tense synonym of showed.

clue.text: Upset editor notices plans

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: signs are notices put up for the public

explanation.surface: An angry editor sees some plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Designs are drawings or schemes for making something, so they are plans; a synonym.

clue.text: Learner in panic beginning to turn red

indicators.note: in says the learner's letter goes inside the word for panic

parts.note: a scare is a sudden panic
L is a learner driver, from the L-plate

indicators.note: beginning to says to take the first letter of the word turn

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A learner driver in a panic starts to blush.
explanation.walkthrough: An L-plate marks a learner driver in Britain, so L stands for learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant shade of red, so the colour word is an example of red.

clue.text: Deer trapping five birds

indicators.note: trapping says the deer enclose the next letter

parts.note: does are female deer
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Deer catching five birds, a strange piece of wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Doves are birds of the pigeon family, so the answer is an example of the plural noun.

clue.text: Model in kimono is revealing back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A model shows off her back in a kimono.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft named no signal for the concealment; 'in' is that signal, pointing into the words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A version is a particular form or variant of something, as a car model is one variant of a range.

clue.text: Resists naughty nurses

indicators.note: naughty says the letters of resists misbehave and take a new order

explanation.surface: Mischievous nurses fight back against something.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse, so sisters are nurses of that rank.

clue.text: Elegant transport going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means read from right to left

parts.note: trams are a form of public transport

explanation.surface: Stylish vehicles heading in a westerly direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart describes being neatly and stylishly dressed, which is what elegant means; a synonym.

clue.text: Darlings certain to be in tears, unfortunately

indicators.note: to be in says the word for certain goes inside the other letters
unfortunately says the letters of tears are in a bad state, rearranged

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Loved ones are sure to be crying, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasures is an affectionate term for much-loved people, used much like darlings.

clue.text: Exam with Open University leaving you grumpy

parts.note: a test is an exam

indicators.note: leaving says those letters depart from the word you

parts.note: OU is the abbreviation for the Open University, the UK distance-learning university

explanation.surface: An exam set by the Open University leaves the student irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy means irritable and short-tempered, a synonym for grumpy.

clue.text: Son caught farm animal on your bike!

definitions.note: British slang for go away, an imperative like the answer

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A son caught a sheep and is told to clear off on his bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On your bike!' is British slang telling someone to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is an informal command to leave at once, the same dismissal as the British phrase.

clue.text: A place for hanging painting only the last character permits

indicators.note: only the last character says to take just the final letter of the word painting

parts.note: its last letter
allows means permits

explanation.surface: A gallery wall that only accepts the very last brushstroke, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A place for hanging painting' looks like a gallery; the definition stops at 'hanging'.
explanation.definitionFit: The gallows is the frame on which criminals were executed by the rope, a place for hanging.

clue.text: Regularly stay by river and eat fish

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter of the word stay

parts.note: its first and third letters
R is the map abbreviation for river
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone often stops by the river to eat fish for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardine is a small oily fish of the herring family, an example of the general word.

clue.text: Please remark about broken fist

indicators.note: about says the word for remark goes round the other letters

parts.note: to say is to remark

indicators.note: broken says the letters of fist are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A request to comment on someone's injured hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please' looks like a polite opener, but it is the verb meaning to gratify.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy someone is to content or gratify them, which is what to please means as a verb.

clue.text: Called about Detective Sergeant's orders

indicators.note: about says the word for called is turned round

parts.note: named means called
DS is the police abbreviation for Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: A police officer is rung up concerning a senior colleague's instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Demands are insistent requests or commands, so as nouns they match orders.
